---
Touches: gateway/scripts/benchmarks-snapshot.sh, gateway/scripts/tiers.py, gateway/specs/endpoints/catalog.md, gateway/tests/test_model_tiers.py
Origin: teststuffstash/homelab#3145
Class: build

---
## Deliverable
`gateway/scripts/benchmarks-snapshot.sh` takes the codex rail's candidates from the gateway's own evidence — the ids `GET /catalog/codex` marks `eligible` (on the enrolled account's catalog, with one clean turn through the gateway) — and the hand-passed `CODEX_CANDIDATES` literal is gone: the variable stays as an override that the snapshot names as such.

Re-ruled by island intake 2026-11-12 on the operator's question "3145 - what is missing from gateway intake handling this?". No ruling is pending: GW-MODEL-TIERS §The rulings already records the rule — codex = "the ENROLLED account's model evidence: its catalog plus one completed turn per id, never a bundled catalog". The "newest of each family" on that line is the dated note of what the 2026-10-29 hand probe covered (four of the eight visible ids), not the rule, and the ask's "∩ the ids the policy can name" below is not the rule either: the policy's lists are DERIVED from the candidates, so they cannot select them. What was missing is the means to execute the recorded rule, now three issues in a chain: the catalog view (#3296, behind Goal #3300) → the entry gate that gives a new id its one turn (#3310) → this derivation. The text as filed is kept verbatim under "As filed".

## Acceptance
1. `benchmarks-snapshot.sh` reads `GET /catalog/codex` and hands `tiers.py --codex-candidates` exactly the `eligible` ids as `codex/<id>`; line 35's literal default (`codex/gpt-6-luna,codex/gpt-6.1-terra,codex/gpt-6.1-sol,codex/gpt-6-astra`) is deleted.
2. `CODEX_CANDIDATES` set → those ids are used and the snapshot records that the codex candidates were an override; unset and the view unreadable → the script exits non-zero naming the read, and writes no snapshot.
3. GW-MODEL-TIERS §The rulings' codex clause and its row "the candidates per rail" say the source is the view's `eligible` ids; the "2026-10-29 the newest of each family" note leaves the rule's sentence (the spike keeps the history).
4. `devbox run tiers -- check` stays green on the committed snapshot: this PR re-cuts nothing.

## Spec changes
Requirement: `GW-MODEL-TIERS` on `specs/endpoints/catalog.md` — §The rulings (binds on the committed snapshot + the deployed policy) and a new section for the script's read, world `policy-codex`.

#### The codex candidates

Legend: `view` = what `GET /catalog/codex` answers the script; `override` = `CODEX_CANDIDATES`.

| description | view | override | candidates? | source? | exit? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the candidates are the view's eligible ids ⚖ | A, B eligible; C candidate; H hidden | unset | codex/A, codex/B | catalog | 0 |
| a visible id without its clean turn is no candidate | A eligible; C candidate | unset | codex/A | catalog | 0 |
| an excluded id is no candidate ⚖ | A eligible; D excluded | unset | codex/A | catalog | 0 |
| the override wins and is named ⚖ | A, B eligible | codex/A,codex/C | codex/A, codex/C | override | 0 |
| an unreadable view fails the snapshot, never a literal ⚖ | the read fails | unset | none | none | non-zero, names the read |
| no eligible id is an empty rail, not a failure ⚖ | C candidate | unset | none | catalog | 0 |

§The rulings, row "the candidates per rail ⚖": the codex clause becomes "codex = the ids the gateway's codex catalog view marks eligible (or the named override), unpriced, every deployed codex id among them".

Index row: unchanged (GW-MODEL-TIERS carries no flag for this).
Unverified: the view's shape and the `state` field are #3296's and #3310's, both unbuilt — the rows above assume `models[].state` as on `/catalog/openrouter`; where the snapshot records `source` (`sources.codex`? — `$defs.benchmarks_snapshot` decides) — verify during implementation; whether the script reaches the view through the port-forward it already opens for the other two catalog reads.

## Out of scope
- The catalog read leg (#3296) and the entry gate (#3310).
- Re-cutting `argocd/resources/agent-gateway/benchmarks.json` and the policy lists — a jail verb and its own PR (GW-MODEL-TIERS' gap "the snapshot is hand-refreshed").
- The weekly AA pull missing release-day models — the cadence note on FU-270.

## As filed (2026-11-01, unchanged)

**Today:** the codex rail's candidates are passed in by hand — `gateway/scripts/benchmarks-snapshot.sh` defaults `CODEX_CANDIDATES` to a literal list (`codex/gpt-6-luna,codex/gpt-6.1-terra,codex/gpt-6.1-sol,codex/gpt-6-astra`, line 31) and `tiers.py --codex-candidates` takes the same string. The other two rails derive their candidates from evidence (GW-CATALOG-OR from the OpenRouter rankings, GW-CATALOG-GO from the Go catalog); the codex rail is the exception, and a model the account gains or loses is invisible until someone edits the string.

**Evidence the leg can read:** the enrolled account's model list is reachable (`/models`, `client_version ≥ 0.155.0`; the 10-23 codex-live fixture is the shape) — the rollout session that lit luna/sol/astra/terra (#3023) confirmed all four completed a real turn on the account.

**Ask:** a `GW-CATALOG-CODEX` leg in `gateway/specs/endpoints/catalog.md` + the snapshot script: candidates = the account's `/models` ∩ the ids the policy can name, refreshed on the same 6 h cadence as the other catalogs; `CODEX_CANDIDATES` becomes an override, not the source. Spec rows + Allure evidence per the pinned process (the island's `gateway/specs`, ADR-156). Related, same handover: the weekly AA capability pull misses release-day models (terra scored 10-26, one day after the pull) — the cadence is a `benchmarks-snapshot.sh` question, noted on FU-270.

**Verified 2026-11-01 (seat):** `devbox run tiers -- check` — every decided list equals the derivation from the 2026-11-01 09:49Z snapshot; terra is in `benchmarks.json` and not in any codex tier, so the derivation (not a stale re-cut) keeps it out today. No open issue matches `codex catalog|CODEX_CANDIDATES` (#3016 closed, luna only).

Source: the pr-open/codex rollout session's handover (item 4), relayed by the seat. Gateway island.
